rule: Append-only. Entries are never edited or removed; later facts are added to an entry's 'updates' list.

versions.title: Version 1 · Does memory help a model solve later tasks?
versions.blurb: A frozen model, a memory of its own mistakes, and a controlled test. Closed on 12 November 2026 with a first real result.

versions.title: Version 1.1 · Research log: learning, forgetting, review and tools
versions.blurb: A simulation-only research log of eight milestones. Small learners we wrote ourselves, no language model, pre-registered hypotheses, failures kept. The code is open source, in the v1.1/ folder of the Lucifer-BenchMarks repository.
open_items: Put the original architecture and USP documents in place and complete the map from the original ideas to V1.1.
Test the ideas with a language model in the loop on the V1 task bank, on a hosted or runner GPU.
Test an attacker who optimises against the reviewers, and add noise or clipping to shared rule vectors.
Run the CI workflow on GitHub, then decide what becomes public.
A variant for the newest MCP revision, and a real browser behind the policy layer.

versions.title: Version 1.2 · Goals: validate with a language model
versions.blurb: The next version. Every V1.1 learning result is a simulation, so these goals test the ideas with a real model, attack the review step and close the gaps V1.1 reported. Nothing here is done yet. Each goal is a GitHub issue with an acceptance test, and each result will be pre-registered before it is run.
versions.page_label: The GitHub milestone for these goals

entries.label: Lab
entries.title: The lab itself
entries.summary: 80 tasks (50 pitfall, 30 hidden-convention) with hidden tests, a sandboxed runner, hash-chained memory with rollback, three conditions, a paired bootstrap and three gates. 125 tests pass.
points: Three conditions on the same model: no memory, Lucifer (relevant lessons) and wrong notes (the least relevant lessons).
Every result is computed from raw rows; nothing is typed in by hand.

entries.label: Calibration
entries.title: A useless first exam, caught early
entries.summary: Strong models scored 96–100% with no memory, so that exam could never show an effect. Calibration said so before any claim was made.
points: A second, harder task set with hidden conventions was written, then calibrated on three model sizes to pick one that can learn from feedback.

entries.label: Scoring bug
entries.title: A scoring bug found by the dashboard
entries.summary: The retention check mistook luck for forgetting (regression to the mean). The dashboard exposed it and the gate's selection was fixed.
points: Tasks are now chosen on half the seeds and measured on the other half.

entries.label: CI/CD
entries.title: Everything moved onto CI/CD
entries.summary: Experiments now run on GitHub Actions: one job per seed, a merge step, gates in the job summary, and published results committed automatically.

entries.label: First real result
entries.title: First real result · Version 1 closed
entries.summary: +50 points first-try success over no memory and over wrong notes, interval +30 to +70, on 5 seeds. Published with every caveat.
points: Model qwen2.5-coder:14b, 30 convention tasks (18 scored), 5 seeds, 630 task runs (1,115 model calls counting retries).
First try on similar and transfer tasks: Lucifer 50% (similar 67%, transfer 17%), no memory 0%, wrong notes 0%.
Gate 1 (improvement) pass, gate 2 (retention) inconclusive because the baseline masters nothing, gate 3 (auditability) pass.
not_shown: One model, 18 scored tasks, tasks written by the author. This is a first look, not proof.

entries.label: Site and proof
entries.title: This site, with a live recompute
entries.summary: Seven detail pages generated from the published rows, a 3D memory chain that uses the real hash formula, and a Proof page that recomputes the headline and its interval in your browser.

entries.label: External review
entries.title: Wording corrected after an outside review
entries.summary: Counts relabelled (630 task runs, 1,115 model calls), absolute claims softened, hash-chain limits stated, stale documentation fixed.
points: A hash chain detects edits when it is checked. It does not prevent them.

entries.label: M1
entries.title: M1 · Read V1 properly and set the rules
entries.summary: V1 was inspected from its code and tests before anything was built, and a rule was fixed for everything after: write the hypotheses and failure conditions first, commit them, then run.
points: V1 is retrieval into a frozen model: its learning step writes text, no weights change. V1's 125 tests pass on a fresh run.

Four weaknesses in V1's memory hash were found and checked by experiment: run id and seed were not covered by the hash, field boundaries could collide, a fully rewritten chain cannot be detected without an outside copy of the head, and the provenance check only tested for non-empty values.
A version 2 hash (every field, length-prefixed, anchor check) fixes them, and V1's own formula is kept so V1 data stays verifiable.
Every later milestone was pre-registered before its code ran. Changes after seeing results are logged as amendments with the reason.
not_shown: The literature review is not done: no reference was read, including the Gupta, Jin and Homma book.
The map from the original Lucifer ideas to V1.1 is not done: the original architecture and USP documents were not available, so nothing here is derived from them.
No formal mathematics beyond the small models in M2 to M5.

updates.text: Later the same day a partial literature review was added: eleven sources confirmed to exist, none read in full, with a note on where V1.1's use differs from each. The map from the original ideas is still not done.

entries.label: M2
entries.title: M2 · Does growing a network help?
entries.summary: A small recurrent network that can grow or be pruned, compared with a fixed network of the same final size. 20 seeds. The answer is no.
points: Safe growth (new units cannot affect old ones) keeps earlier tasks exactly (error change 8e-17) but ends far worse than a fixed network of equal size: error 0.417 against 0.068.
Growth that rewires everything is as capable but wipes the old readouts: earlier-task error went from 0.04 to 195.
Growth saved no compute, and pruning by importance was no better than random pruning.
The first run was uninformative (every network failed because the task was too hard); it was kept, the fix was logged as an amendment, and the task difficulty was set using fixed networks only.
not_shown: A toy simulation. It does not say dynamic networks cannot work, only that this design gave no benefit and was not adopted.

head: Check
Verdict
Evidence
rows: Safe growth matches a fixed net of equal size
Growth beats the small fixed net

entries.label: M3
entries.title: M3 · A hybrid executive: what each part is worth
entries.summary: Four separable mechanisms (a protected goal slot, a failure monitor, learned reliability estimates, cost-aware choice) in a designed world, each removed in turn.
points: In the combined world the executive completed 0.79 more episodes than a plain router.
Each part helped only where its failure mode exists: protected goals under interruptions (+0.77), the monitor under failures (+0.24), learned estimates after drift (+0.28).
Overhead is real: 4 to 6 control steps per episode; in a world where nothing can fail the executive adds 4.2 steps and 0.21 extra cost for zero gain.
Two of three registered checks failed: my 'benign' world still had 3% failures, and cost-aware choice saved 0.40 cost units against the 0.5 I had registered.
not_shown: The world and the executive were both written by us, so effect sizes follow our parameters. This does not show planning or reasoning.

head: Check
Verdict
Evidence
rows: No gain in a benign world
Each part helps only where needed

entries.label: M4
entries.title: M4 · Learning from experience, and forgetting
entries.summary: Retrieval, parameter adaptation and two protections against forgetting on one stream of 12 contexts, 30 seeds. The log of experience is kept separate from learning.
points: Forgetting is real: the plain learner forgot 0.159 of what it had learned.
A consolidation anchor (a pull toward the previous weights) cut forgetting from 0.159 to 0.021 with no raw experience stored, at a cost of 0.014 accuracy.
Replay of a 100-example buffer made forgetting slightly worse; it needed 300 to 960 stored examples to help, which conflicts with keeping raw experience local.
Logging an experience does not change the model; replaying the learning log reproduces training exactly; deleting a record does not unlearn it, rebuilding from a checkpoint without it does.
The registered check that experience speeds up learning new contexts failed on its first-10-examples measure (see M8 for a different measure).
not_shown: A small simulated learner. Nothing about language models.

entries.label: M5
entries.title: M5 · A parent and independent children
entries.summary: An in-process parent coordinator and children that each keep their own raw data. The parent receives only metadata: hashes, names, numbers.
points: Registration, message authentication, replay protection, a strict allow-list of fields, anchored audits of each child's history, and checkpoint integrity: 31 tests, 6 of 6 deliberate breakages caught.
When two tenants' rules conflict, a model per tenant beat one shared model by 0.147; when the rules agree, sharing gained only 0.009 (the registered 0.02 was missed).
A written threat model lists what is not covered: real key management, transport security, covert channels and inference from parameters.
not_shown: A prototype in one process. It is not evidence that a deployed system is secure.

head: Check
Verdict
Evidence
rows: Personal beats shared when rules conflict

entries.label: M6
entries.title: M6 · Reviewing knowledge before it is shared
entries.summary: A package is the decision rule one child learned for one context. Review combines metadata checks with evaluation by other children on their own private data; promotions are versioned and reversible.
points: Valid metadata proves nothing about benefit: all 180 poisoned packages passed the metadata checks. The full review accepted none of them (0 of 180, which bounds the true rate only to about 1.7%).
It also blocked 28% of honest, useful packages (72% accepted; the registered target was 80%), and blocked all tenant-specific ones.
A poor tenant gained 0.109 accuracy on the contexts where knowledge agreed; blindly adopting everything lost 0.10 to 0.15.
Promotion and rollback are entries on a hash chain; rolling back restores the exact earlier state and keeps the archived entries.
not_shown: Not tested: an attacker who optimises against the reviewers' data, colluding reviewers, and whether a shared rule vector leaks information about the data it came from.

head: Check
Verdict
Evidence
rows: Review blocks poison; metadata alone fails

entries.label: M7
entries.title: M7 · Own tool engine, with MCP and A2A on top
entries.summary: A tool engine that denies by default, validates input and output, rate-limits, times out, requires one-time approvals for external effects and audits every call without storing raw data.
points: The MCP adapter was checked against the current specification first: the newest revision (2026-07-28) removed the old handshake. The adapter speaks the earlier handshake era and was tested against the official Python client in two modes, which listed, called and received tool errors correctly. The newest revision is not supported and not claimed.

A runtime with retries, back-off and crash recovery that never repeats finished work; an in-process model of the agent-to-agent task lifecycle; a browser policy layer that refuses look-alike addresses, never fills passwords or card numbers, and needs a one-time approval to submit.
193 tests; 21 of 22 deliberate breakages caught (the 22nd changes nothing, by construction).
not_shown: The A2A part is a model, not the wire protocol. The browser layer ran against a fake browser. Tool code is not sandboxed.

entries.label: M8
entries.title: M8 · Everything rerun, two gaps closed, one report
entries.summary: Two hypotheses nobody had tested (maturation and unseen task families) were tested, and every experiment was rerun from scratch to confirm the verdicts.
points: Maturation (less plasticity, more consolidation with age) halved forgetting but lost 0.027 accuracy, outside the registered tolerance: failed.
Experience helped on new contexts of the same family (+0.065) but was not shown safe on a different family (−0.022, interval touching zero): failed as registered.

Everything reran in 67 seconds: all 23 verdict flags identical and no numeric difference. Measured overhead: the tool engine adds about 176 microseconds per call; an audit entry costs 2.65 microseconds.
Scoreboard: 21 registered threshold hypotheses, 10 passed and 11 failed, with no threshold ever moved; every property check passed.
not_shown: No language model was involved anywhere in V1.1. V1's retrieval result remains the only real-model evidence.

updates.text: Merged into the open-source Lucifer-BenchMarks repository under v1.1/, with its full commit history (pull request 1). Version 1's CI and the new V1.1 tests are green on Python 3.11 and 3.13. The GitHub milestone for V1.1 is closed; the next goals are tracked in milestone V1.2.

entries.label: Proof
entries.title: Proof of existence
entries.summary: Two manifests list the SHA-256 of every file: V1 (56 files, commit fe08665) and the finished V1.1 work (89 files, commit ce5ed13). Each manifest's own hash was submitted to OpenTimestamps.
points: V1 manifest root: 9cbfd13f6f69466421062a2a7e636dd54d4cc0cc0f97be17632741c9fc163bc2 (file SHA-256 ac3c4ffcde6e9c152acb52fbeb48495898d8e71bd4e8facc2e773dccc4d37827).
V1.1 manifest root: 47876d17f55587caaa159ef0b82b739f35863efd24d7a41aac27e25f41d2efe2 (file SHA-256 f85c2af4a038f227bb34bf3119c15ad9e14b81ab1727a0fca135f76ef4edd35e).
Status at publication: both stamps are pending a Bitcoin confirmation (hours). When they confirm, an update is appended below; nothing here is edited.
To check: put the manifest and its .ots file in one folder and run ots verify on the .ots file.
not_shown: A timestamp shows a file existed by a date. It does not show who wrote it, and it is not a patent or a copyright registration. The code and raw results are in the v1.1/ folder of the open-source Lucifer-BenchMarks repository, with their full commit history; both manifests verify against that repository.

updates.text: Both manifests verify against the Benchmarks repository (89 and 56 files, 0 mismatches). The OpenTimestamps stamps are still pending a Bitcoin confirmation.

Both stamps are now confirmed in Bitcoin: the V1 manifest in block 975752 (06:32 UTC) and the V1.1 manifest in blocks 975759 and 975761 (07:17 and 07:18 UTC). Checked independently: each stamp commits to its manifest's SHA-256, and the Merkle root it attests equals the block header's Merkle root on a public block explorer. The stamp files linked above were replaced with the confirmed versions.

entries.label: Goal 1
entries.title: Test parameter-level adaptation against V1's retrieval with a language model
entries.summary: On the V1 task bank, compare V1 retrieval, a small adapter or lesson-conditioned fine-tune, and both, on held-out tasks, 5 seeds.
points: Why: every V1.1 learning result is a simulation, and V1's retrieval gain is retrieval into a prompt, not learning.
Acceptance: hypotheses and failure conditions committed before the run, raw rows published, failures reported. Needs a GPU on a hosted service or a CI runner.

entries.label: Goal 2
entries.title: Build an adaptive attacker against the review step
entries.summary: The review blocked 0 of 180 fixed poisoned packages, but that attacker did not adapt to the reviewers' data.
points: Craft packages optimised against the reviewers' validation data, then try colluding reviewers.
Acceptance: attack code and a pre-registered acceptance-rate result, published whether or not the review holds.

entries.label: Goal 3
entries.title: Rule-vector privacy: membership inference, clipping and noise
entries.summary: Shared decision-rule vectors may reveal something about the data they were learned from; no noise or clipping is applied yet.
points: Measure leakage from a shared rule vector, then add clipping or noise and measure the utility cost.
Acceptance: a pre-registered leakage metric, a utility-versus-privacy table and tests.

entries.label: Goal 4
entries.title: Check whether V1 tasks ident-4 and ident-6 are solvable
entries.summary: Two V1 tasks were never solved first try in any seed (0 of 5) and may be unfair; this was flagged but never tested.
points: Check whether a person can infer the convention from the spec plus one failing-test message.
Acceptance: a short report; if the tasks are unfair, fix or retire them and note the effect on the V1 numbers. A good first issue.

entries.label: Goal 5
entries.title: Scale V1: a second model, at least 48 primary tasks, a held-out task family
entries.summary: V1 used one model and 18 scored tasks; its own power table says about 48 are needed to detect smaller effects.
points: Add hidden-convention tasks (not renamed copies), run a second model through the existing backends, and design one family before looking at results.
Acceptance: the same pipeline, published rows, intervals and not only means.

entries.label: Goal 6
entries.title: MCP server for the 2026-07-28 revision
entries.summary: The tool server speaks the earlier handshake era; the newest MCP revision removed the handshake, so modern-only clients cannot use it.
points: Add a modern-era variant that reuses the tool engine.
Acceptance: the test that documents the current limit is replaced by a passing test against the official client pinned to that revision.

entries.label: Goal 7
entries.title: A real browser behind the browser policy layer
entries.summary: The browser layer is a policy layer tested only against a fake driver.
points: Implement the driver with a real browser as an optional dependency and add an adversarial page corpus (look-alike origins, redirects, hidden fields, prompt-injection text).
Acceptance: the policy tests pass against the real driver, plus a pre-registered result on the corpus.

entries.label: Goal 8
entries.title: Test conditional computation and routing against a fixed network
entries.summary: The literature review found that most dynamic-network work is data-dependent computation; V1.1 tested growth and pruning, not that.
points: Pre-register a routing or early-exit test against a parameter-matched fixed network.
Acceptance: pre-registration first, then a published result.

entries.label: Goal 9
entries.title: Read the cited sources in full and fill the literature gaps
entries.summary: The literature review lists eleven sources confirmed to exist but read only at abstract level, and leaves several topics out.
points: Read the sources, correct any claim the text does not support, and add the missing areas with verified citations.
Acceptance: every entry marked read or not read; no citation without a checked source.

entries.label: Goal 10
entries.title: Map the original Lucifer ideas to V1.1
entries.summary: A maintainer task that needs the original architecture and USP documents, which are not in the repository. Nothing will be invented to fill the gap.
points: For each original concept: preserved, implemented, partly implemented, needs formalisation, redesign, deferred, or rejected with a reason.
Acceptance: a table where each row cites the source document it came from.

achievements.title: A first real result, with every caveat
achievements.text: Version 1: +50 points first-try success over no memory and over wrong notes (interval +30 to +70), one model, 5 seeds, 630 task runs.

achievements.title: A result you can recompute in your browser
achievements.text: The Proof page recomputes the headline and its interval from the raw rows, and the 3D memory chain uses the real hash formula.

achievements.title: Eight milestones, hypotheses written first, failures kept
achievements.text: Version 1.1: 21 registered threshold hypotheses, 10 passed and 11 failed, with no threshold moved; every property check passed.

achievements.title: Everything reproduces from scratch
achievements.text: 202 tests; a fresh rerun of the experiments matched all 23 verdict flags with a maximum numeric difference of 0, in 67 seconds, on the author's Mac.

achievements.title: Interoperates with the official MCP client
achievements.text: The tool server was tested against the official Python client in two modes. The newest protocol revision is not supported and not claimed.

achievements.title: CI is green on GitHub, Python 3.11 and 3.13
achievements.text: Both Version 1's own workflow and the new V1.1 workflow passed on the merged pull request.

achievements.title: Open source, with open goals
achievements.text: V1.1 is merged into the Benchmarks repository with its full history, and the next ten goals are GitHub issues in an open milestone, with a contributing guide.

achievements.title: A dated, checkable record of the files
achievements.text: Hashes of every file (V1: 56 files, V1.1: 89 files) were submitted for OpenTimestamps and verify against the repository. Bitcoin confirmation is pending; a timestamp shows existence by a date, not authorship.

achievements.title: Both file lists are anchored in Bitcoin
achievements.text: The hashes of every file of Version 1 (56 files) and Version 1.1 (89 files) are recorded in Bitcoin blocks 975752, 975759 and 975761 through OpenTimestamps, and checked against the block headers. This shows the files existed by then. It does not show who wrote them.
